# go-modern-atomic-types

**Since:** Go 1.19

## Summary

Use typed atomics such as atomic.Bool, atomic.Int64, and `atomic.Pointer[T]` instead of untyped atomic functions.

## Details

Typed atomic wrapper values keep the storage and the atomic operations together.
They make the value type visible, reduce accidental non-atomic access, and avoid old pointer-alignment pitfalls.

## Examples

### Example 1

### Before

```go
var enabled int32
atomic.StoreInt32(&enabled, 1)
if atomic.LoadInt32(&enabled) != 0 {
  run()
}
```

### After

```go
var enabled atomic.Bool
enabled.Store(true)
if enabled.Load() {
  run()
}
```

### Example 2

### Before 2

```go
var ptr unsafe.Pointer
atomic.StorePointer(&ptr, unsafe.Pointer(cfg))
```

### After 2

```go
var ptr atomic.Pointer[Config]
ptr.Store(cfg)
```
